title: Clarinet Concerto in A major
hook: Mozart’s last concerto, written for a friend’s clarinet weeks before he died.

painting.title: Italian Landscape with Mountains and a River
painting.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (Sarah Campbell Blaffer Foundation)
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years from Wright’s memories of Italy, it has the concerto’s warm, late light and its unhurried calm, with a shadow at the edges.

facts: Mozart finished the concerto in October 1791, about two months before his death. It is his last concerto and one of the last works he completed.

He wrote it for his friend Anton Stadler, a Viennese clarinettist, who played a special instrument with extra low notes: the [[basset-clarinet|basset clarinet]]. Mozart’s own score is lost. When the concerto was first printed, around 1801, the solo part was rewritten for the ordinary clarinet, and many of the lowest passages were moved up.
The first movement grew out of an unfinished concerto for basset horn, a larger relative of the clarinet, that Mozart had abandoned after about 200 bars.
The orchestra is light: two flutes, two bassoons, two horns and strings. There are no oboes, trumpets or drums.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a warm, spacious Allegro (I), a slow song of great simplicity (II), a playful rondo with shadows (III).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A broad, sunny first movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a [[double-exposition|double exposition]]: the orchestra plays the main tunes first, then the clarinet enters and makes them its own. The clarinet sings, but it also leaps from its bright top notes to its dark, woody bottom notes, as if two characters were talking.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a warm, gently rocking tune in the strings, soon taken up by the whole orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The clarinet’s range
mainIdeas.description: sudden leaps between high and very low notes, and fast runs that sweep across the whole instrument.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a quieter, more wistful tune that the clarinet introduces in the solo exposition.

stops.hear: The strings play a calm, warm tune; the whole orchestra follows
stops.happening: Theme 1, the orchestra’s exposition. No soloist yet

stops.hear: The clarinet enters with the opening tune
Running notes that sweep from the top of the clarinet to its deepest notes
stops.happening: The clarinet shows its range, including the extra low notes of the basset clarinet

stops.hear: The clarinet plays a quieter, more wistful tune; the harmony clouds over, then clears
The orchestra alone, loud and confident
The clarinet returns in a minor key, with leaps and broken chords over a soft accompaniment
The warm opening tune returns in the home key

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The orchestra alone rounds off the movement
stops.happening: The closing tutti. Mozart left no place for a big solo [[cadenza|cadenza]]

notice: Listen for the clarinet’s low notes. Ordinary clarinets cannot play the lowest of them; Thea King plays a basset clarinet, the instrument Mozart wrote for.
When the clarinet leaps from high to low, it can sound like a question and an answer from two different voices.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A slow song in three parts. The clarinet sings a simple melody, the orchestra repeats it, and a freer middle section lets the clarinet roam across its range before the melody returns.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a slow, simple melody in the clarinet over soft strings.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: longer, more ornamented lines that dip into the clarinet’s low register.

stops.hear: The clarinet sings a slow, simple melody over quiet strings
The orchestra plays the same melody, fuller and warmer
The clarinet’s line becomes freer, with wider leaps and quick decorations
The music pauses; the clarinet leads back alone with a few free notes
stops.happening: A short link back to the main theme

stops.hear: The opening melody returns in the clarinet, very quietly
stops.happening: The return of the main theme

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Clarinet and orchestra close softly together

notice: The melody moves mostly by small steps and repeated notes. Its beauty comes from the clarinet’s tone and breathing more than from any surprise.

movements.heading: Rondo: Allegro
movements.summary: A lively finale in a skipping six-beat rhythm. It is a [[rondo|rondo]]: the clarinet’s bouncing refrain keeps coming back, with episodes in between, and one of them turns unexpectedly dark.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a cheerful, bouncing tune, played first by the clarinet and then by the orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The episodes
mainIdeas.description: quick runs and leaps for the clarinet, and one passage in a minor key that clouds the mood.

stops.hear: The clarinet plays a bouncing, skipping tune
The orchestra repeats it, louder
The clarinet races away with runs and wide leaps
The bouncing tune returns
The mood darkens: a minor key, the clarinet low and serious
stops.happening: The second episode, the most shadowed part of the finale

stops.hear: The bouncing tune again
The music of the first episode returns, now in the home key

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The refrain one last time, then a brisk close

notice: Notice how quickly the music can turn from playful to serious and back. The dark episode lasts only a minute or so.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Thea King plays a basset clarinet in a version of the solo part that restores Mozart’s low notes, based on Alan Hacker’s reconstruction.

threads.title: A voice with two registers
threads.body: In every movement the clarinet moves between its bright upper notes and its dark lower ones.

threads.title: Singing
threads.body: The Adagio is a song without words, and the outer movements keep returning to long, singing lines.

threads.title: Shadows in the sun
threads.body: Each movement is mainly bright, but each has a moment where the music darkens.
